body:
## Problem

A stack-mode flow run that holds a bundle and finishes everything else exits 0. The held bundle's work is on no line of the run, and the only signal is a couple of stderr lines. A script or CI job calling `pdca flow` cannot tell that run apart from a clean one.

`_results_rc` returns 0 when every bundle is COMPLETE/RESOLVED (`template/src/pdca_harness/cli.py:679-690`). A held bundle is COMPLETE: it was built and published, and only the fold left it out. Two holds produce this:

- the #593 `held_unpushed` hold (a bundle that pushed no branch this run, `flow.py:2134`, `:2332-2341`);
- the #674 same-wave conflict hold (PR #690, not yet merged), when the held bundle has no in-batch dependents.

Before #674, the same batch stopped at the fold and exited 1.

## Evidence (eduralph/pdca-pdca, issue_674, signed off 2026-10-14)

The reviewer ran two batches on the patched tree: `10`/`11` conflicting on `shared.txt`, plus `12` and `21`/`22` (`Depends on: 12`). Every result was COMPLETE and `_results_rc` returned 0. The only sign that 11's work is on no line, and that its draft PR conflicts with 10's, was two stderr lines. It is listed in PR #690's "Known limits" and in the bundle's §10.

## Possible fixes

1. Give a run that held any bundle a distinct non-zero exit code (for example 3, "finished with holds"), documented next to the #468 exit-code rule.
2. Or mark the held bundle in its results/state so `pdca status` and callers see it, and keep rc 0.

## Done when

A caller can tell from the exit code (or one documented machine-readable marker) that a run held a bundle, for both the #593 and #674 holds. A test pins it.

Raised by the eduralph/pdca-pdca Act review of 2026-10-14.
title: flow: a run that holds a bundle (#593 unpushed, #674 conflict) exits 0, so scripts and CI can't tell
